description:
## Summary

The runner today admits https/ssh/git working copies and injects forge credentials into containers under connector-era assumptions. Radicle-native Groundwork needs sessions that hold a Radicle working copy and act as their own bounded contributor identity, created inside the session boundary — the operator's delegate key never enters a session. This mirrors the existing per-agent SSH identity discipline, with the key generated in-boundary instead of mounted into it.

Part of: tesserine/groundwork#538 (execution-boundary enablement).

## Scope

- Runner repo-URL validation surface
- Session identity provisioning (per-session/per-agent Radicle profile inside the container)
- Runbooks and docs

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A session can be dispatched on a Radicle-sourced working copy: the repo-URL surface admits the Radicle form and the runner materializes a working copy from it.
- [ ] Each session operates as its own Radicle identity created inside the session boundary, holding contributor authority only; no operator or delegate key material is mounted, copied, or injected; `RAD_PASSPHRASE`-in-environment is not used as a custody mechanism.
- [ ] State authored by a session replicates per the declared seeding policy, verified by read-back from a project-controlled node.
- [ ] Existing non-Radicle transports keep working unchanged; runbooks/docs cover the provisioning pattern alongside the per-agent SSH identity runbook.

## Contract inputs

- **Behavior:** a dispatched session on a Radicle working copy authors an issue or patch that a project-controlled node then holds — demonstrated end to end.
- **Documentation:** the runbook is where a deployer first meets Radicle session provisioning; it states the custody boundary explicitly.
- **Code quality:** the custody mandate is a hard boundary — no weakening for convenience (tesserine/groundwork#538 standing constraints).

## Dependencies

Depends on: tesserine/groundwork#599 (the custody and replication policy this enforces), tesserine/base#26 (the toolchain sessions run). Kin: the babbie-ops node unit (the network sessions replicate to).
